title: reservation-triggered-throttle-and-utilization-wavelet-reporter
author: Priya Patel
description: Context: Dedicated fleets sometimes oscillate between being underutilized and briefly saturated during short bursts. Existing burst controls rely on global accounting windows which either respond too late or over-aggressively for reservation-backed traffic. This PR introduces a reservation-triggered throttle that activates when a reservation's consumption pattern crosses configurable safety thresholds, and a complementary utilization wavelet reporter that provides smoothed, multi-scale utilization signals for autoscalers and SLO monitors. Motivation: reduce noisy evictions and over-provisioning, improve SLO preservation for reservation-backed tenants, and provide more actionable utilization telemetry for downstream controllers. What this changes: 1) Runtime: add a reservation-level throttle controller that monitors per-reservation token/slot consumption and emits soft-throttle decisions when short-timescale spike characteristics exceed the reservation's burst envelope. The throttle is implemented as a cooperative gate (non-destructive) that reduces accepted concurrency and gates new burst credits for the reservation while preserving headroom for latency-sensitive requests. 2) Telemetry: introduce the "util.wavelet" metric family which reports wavelet-decomposed utilization bands (fast/medium/slow) plus a peakiness score used by the autoscaler. Wavelet decomposition uses a lightweight Haar-ish discrete transform tuned for 1s/10s/60s bands to avoid heavy CPU overhead. 3) Config and rollout: feature-gated behind experimental-reservation-throttle; tunable knobs exposed in Dedicated config (burst_window_ms, peakiness_threshold, soft_throttle_factor, wavelet_bands). 4) Observability: dashboards and burn-down charts added to console for reservation-level throttle events, plus alerts and appetite tests. 5) Tests: unit tests for gate logic, integration tests validating no regression for shared-fleet tenants, and a load canary validating that throttled reservations do not cascade. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2231) - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Telemetry dashboards PR (docs/observability) - [x] Feature gate and rollout plan - [x] Load canary results attached (canary-2026-02-22) Rollout plan: start with 1% of reservations in a single region with telemetry-only enabled, then enable soft-throttle for a week with conservative thresholds before gradual scale to 25% and evaluating eviction rates and tail latency. If tail latencies increase for shared non-reserved tenants, revert soft-throttle and iterate. Related: builds on earlier utilization smoothing work (ENG-2209) and is complementary to global burst-bank refactors.

review_comments: Marcus Green: This looks solid — can you clarify the CPU cost of the wavelet decomposition at 100k series/sec?

Author (Priya Patel): We budgeted ~0.7 CPU per 100k series when sampled at 1s resolution; wavelet uses incremental sliding windows and is N log N with a very small constant (Haar-like). Added benchmarks to wavelet_reporter.go and documented the numbers.
Ava Chen: We need a clearer failure mode when the throttle gate misfires and blocks warmup traffic. Add a failsafe that allows N recovery tokens per minute.
Author (Priya Patel): Added recovery token mechanism and test coverage; included kill-switch config and alerting for >0.1% false positives.
Diego Morales: Minor: prefer cfg.BurstWindowMs to be in seconds in config files for readability. Also add a migration note for existing dedicated configs.
Author (Priya Patel): Switched to seconds in dedicated_defaults.yaml and added migration block in docs and a config linter warning.
release_notes: Introduces reservation-triggered soft throttle to reduce noisy evictions and a new util.wavelet telemetry that provides multi-timescale utilization bands and a peakiness score for autoscalers. Feature gated behind experimental-reservation-throttle; disabled by default.
notes_for_ops: When enabling in prod, start telemetry-only, watch util.wavelet.fast and peakiness. Recommended conservative soft_throttle_factor=0.5 and peakiness_threshold=0.8 for initial rollout. Alert on throttle_event_rate > 0.5% and false_positive_rate > 0.1%.
canary_reference: canary-2026-02-22: reservation sample set (region-us-west-2), observed 18% reduction in eviction churn for reservation-backed tenants and <2% impact on shared tenants' p99 latency.
security_review: no changes to auth; telemetry uses existing metrics exporter and respects PII filters
